title: QA_Platform_pr_lines_cannot_be_pulled_into_a_published_event
preconditions: The sandbox event {{eventGroupUuid}} is PUBLISHED (status active, bid window open, no bids). Caller is the run's QA buyer (has trade create_record). {{prItemId}} is a REAL PR line; the request is refused before any write.
steps: 1. POST /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/pri_to_draft_project with the exact body the PR screen's 'Add Items' button sends (status draft, quantity 1 Nos, product, quality, pr_line_item_uuid = a real PR line).
2. Read the status code and error.
3. GET /purchase_requests/{{prId}} - the line's open quantity is unchanged.
expectedResult: HTTP 422, error.code 2 'Insufficient parameters'. The controller only looks for the target among DRAFT events of the workspace (EventGroup.draft.where(id:, company_id:)) and the sandbox is active, so the lookup is nil and the blank guard fires (app/controllers/api/event_groups_controller.rb:1009-1011) before EventGroups::PrToErfxService is even constructed. No line item, PR mapping or draft-quantity reservation is written.
rationale: Adding PR lines is only defined for drafts; a live event must never silently grow new PR-backed lines (vendors would be bidding on a sheet that changed under them, and the PR would show quantity reserved by an event that never asked for it). Also shows the existing PR-EVT-005 cannot reach the 557 rung it claims - the draft guard answers first.

title: QA_Platform_pull_into_unknown_event_is_refused
preconditions: A well-formed uuid that decodes to event id 999999999 (no such row). Caller is the QA buyer. PR reference is also bogus, so nothing real is touched even if a guard regressed.
steps: 1. POST /event_groups/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/pri_to_draft_project with a valid-shaped line.
2. Read the status code and error.
expectedResult: HTTP 422, error.code 2 'Insufficient parameters' - ParamsAuth#check_for_uuid decodes the path id to 999999999, the draft lookup returns nil and the blank guard fires (app/controllers/api/event_groups_controller.rb:1009-1011). Not a 404 and not a 500.
rationale: A missing event must give the same typed refusal as a non-draft one; a 404/500 here would mean the guard order changed and the service is being constructed with a nil event_group (pr_to_erfx_service.rb:13 calls @event_group.company).

title: QA_Platform_pull_by_raw_numeric_event_id_is_refused
preconditions: Caller is the QA buyer. Path carries a raw integer id instead of a uuid; PR reference is bogus.
steps: 1. POST /event_groups/999999999/pri_to_draft_project with a valid-shaped line.
2. Read the status code and error.
expectedResult: HTTP 422, error.code 2 'Insufficient parameters'. An integer-looking id skips uuid decoding unless the uuid-enabled version flag is set (params_auth.rb:60-63); either way the lookup is scoped to company_id = Current.workspace.id and status draft, so a raw id of another tenant's draft is indistinguishable from a missing one (app/controllers/api/event_groups_controller.rb:1009-1011).
rationale: Raw ids are the classic IDOR probe. The answer must not differ between 'exists elsewhere' and 'does not exist', and must never reach the service.

title: QA_Platform_pull_with_line_items_as_object_is_refused_not_crashed
preconditions: The sandbox event {{eventGroupUuid}} is PUBLISHED (status active, bid window open, no bids). Caller is the run's QA buyer (has trade create_record).
steps: 1. POST to the sandbox's pri_to_draft_project with line_items sent as a JSON object instead of an array.
2. Read the status code and error.
expectedResult: HTTP 422, error.code 2 'Insufficient parameters' (app/controllers/api/event_groups_controller.rb:1009-1011). Note for a DRAFT target the same body would reach EventGroups::PrToErfxService.new, whose constructor calls @line_items_data.pluck(:pr_line_item_id) OUTSIDE the service's rescue (pr_to_erfx_service.rb:12,96) - ActionController::Parameters has no pluck, so that path would 500; this case pins that the published-event guard still answers first.
rationale: Type confusion on the main array. Guards the guard order: any refactor that moves the service construction above the draft lookup turns this into an untyped 500.

title: QA_Platform_pull_with_line_items_as_string_is_refused_not_crashed
preconditions: The sandbox event {{eventGroupUuid}} is PUBLISHED (status active, bid window open, no bids). Caller is the run's QA buyer (has trade create_record).
steps: 1. POST to the sandbox's pri_to_draft_project with line_items set to a plain string.
2. Read the status code and error.
expectedResult: HTTP 422, error.code 2 'Insufficient parameters' (app/controllers/api/event_groups_controller.rb:1009-1011); the string is non-blank so only the draft lookup stops it. On a draft target String#pluck would raise NoMethodError before the service's begin/rescue (pr_to_erfx_service.rb:96) - an untyped 500.
rationale: Second shape of the same type confusion; cheap insurance that the refusal stays typed.

title: QA_Platform_pull_with_line_items_of_strings_is_refused_not_crashed
preconditions: The sandbox event {{eventGroupUuid}} is PUBLISHED (status active, bid window open, no bids). Caller is the run's QA buyer (has trade create_record).
steps: 1. POST to the sandbox's pri_to_draft_project with line_items = an array of two strings.
2. Read the status code and error.
expectedResult: HTTP 422, error.code 2 'Insufficient parameters' (app/controllers/api/event_groups_controller.rb:1009-1011). On a draft target Array#pluck would call String#[](:pr_line_item_id) and raise TypeError in the constructor (pr_to_erfx_service.rb:96) - outside the rescue, so a 500.
rationale: Element-level type confusion; the constructor-time pluck is unguarded, so the published/unknown-event refusal is the only thing standing between this body and a crash.

title: QA_Platform_pull_cannot_rehome_a_live_events_own_line
preconditions: The sandbox event {{eventGroupUuid}} is PUBLISHED (status active, bid window open, no bids). Caller is the run's QA buyer (has trade create_record). {{lineItemUuid}} is one of the sandbox's own (active) line items.
steps: 1. POST to the sandbox's pri_to_draft_project with one line that carries uuid = {{lineItemUuid}} (an existing live line) plus a bogus PR reference.
2. Read the status code and error.
3. GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_line_items - the line is still there, still active.
expectedResult: HTTP 422, error.code 2 'Insufficient parameters' (app/controllers/api/event_groups_controller.rb:1009-1011). Context: on a DRAFT target, EventGroups::UpdateService#create_line_items looks the sent id up with EventGroupLineItem.where(id: ...) WITHOUT scoping to the target event (update_service.rb:99,111-113) and then rewrites that row's event_group and status - so the draft guard is what keeps a live line from being moved here. Nothing may change on the sandbox.
rationale: Probes the most dangerous field in this body (line uuid). If the draft guard ever regressed, a buyer could pull a running event's line - including another tenant's - into their own draft.

title: QA_Platform_negative_quantity_on_published_event_is_refused
preconditions: The sandbox event {{eventGroupUuid}} is PUBLISHED (status active, bid window open, no bids). Caller is the run's QA buyer (has trade create_record).
steps: 1. POST to the sandbox's pri_to_draft_project with quantity.value = -5 on a PR line.
2. Read the status code and error.
expectedResult: HTTP 422, error.code 2 'Insufficient parameters' (app/controllers/api/event_groups_controller.rb:1009-1011). Context: on a draft, validate_purchase_request_items_data only checks adding_quantity > max_allowed (event_group_controller_helper.rb:85-86), so -5 would pass validation - see API-XDPRE-027.
rationale: Documents that negative quantities are only stopped here by the state guard, not by any quantity rule.

title: QA_Platform_large_batch_into_published_event_is_refused_cheaply
preconditions: The sandbox event {{eventGroupUuid}} is PUBLISHED (status active, bid window open, no bids). Caller is the run's QA buyer (has trade create_record).
steps: 1. POST to the sandbox's pri_to_draft_project with 100 lines (all bogus PR references).
2. Read the status code, error and response time.
expectedResult: HTTP 422, error.code 2 'Insufficient parameters' quickly (app/controllers/api/event_groups_controller.rb:1009-1011) - no per-line work happens before the draft lookup. There is no line-count cap anywhere on this endpoint (unlike partial_close's 20).
rationale: A large cart must still be refused in constant time on a non-draft; also records that the endpoint has no batch-size limit.

title: QA_Platform_purchase_cart_params_refused_for_published_event
preconditions: The sandbox event {{eventGroupUuid}} is PUBLISHED (status active, bid window open, no bids). Caller is the run's QA buyer (has trade create_record).
steps: 1. GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/purchase_cart_params.
2. Read the status code and error.
expectedResult: HTTP 422, error.code 2 'Insufficient parameters' - the same draft-only lookup (EventGroup.draft.where(id:, company_id:)) as pri_to_draft_project (app/controllers/api/event_groups_controller.rb:1022-1027). No data returned.
rationale: The cart-params read is the companion of 'Add to draft'; it must agree that a live event is not a cart.

title: QA_Platform_purchase_cart_params_refused_for_unknown_event
preconditions: A well-formed uuid for event id 999999999 (no such row).
steps: 1. GET /event_groups/Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==/purchase_cart_params.
2. Read the status code and error.
expectedResult: HTTP 422, error.code 2 'Insufficient parameters' (app/controllers/api/event_groups_controller.rb:1024-1026); authorize is never reached so no 455/500.
rationale: Unknown id must not leak existence or crash the Pundit call with a nil record.

title: QA_Platform_draft_picker_listing_view_reads_cleanly
preconditions: Caller is the QA buyer. Read only.
steps: 1. GET /event_groups/draft?listing_view=true (the call the 'Add to Draft Project' picker makes).
2. Assert no 5xx; every listed event group is a draft that already has a purchase request linked.
expectedResult: HTTP 200. With listing_view=true the action keeps only drafts whose purchase_requests association is present (app/controllers/api/event_groups_controller.rb:350-352), so a draft created without PR lines - or one whose PR lines have not been mapped yet - never shows in the picker. Never a 5xx.
rationale: This list decides which drafts a buyer can add PR lines to; a crash here blocks the whole Add-to-draft flow.

title: QA_Platform_create_with_nonexistent_pr_line_does_not_crash
preconditions: Caller is the QA buyer; {{productUuid}}/{{productQualityUuid}} are the client's catalog product. The request creates a NEW QA_Platform_ draft only; the PR reference is bogus so no real PR is touched.
steps: 1. POST /event_groups with a working draft body whose single line carries pr_line_item_uuid = Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw== (PR line 999999999, does not exist).
2. Read the status code; if 200, note the returned line items.
expectedResult: No 5xx. Today the create is ACCEPTED: EventGroups::CreateService never checks that pr_line_item_id exists - the dormant gate and set_pr_details both query company-scoped PR items and silently find none (create_service.rb:69-90,103-115), and the id is copied into the line's meta_data (trade_controller_helper.rb:6330). The draft carries a dangling PR reference that only fails later, at stage creation (557, trade_controller_helper.rb:1737-1748). A 422 code 557 would be the better answer.
rationale: Pins current behaviour and flags the gap: a PR-based draft can be created against a PR line that does not exist, which only surfaces when the buyer tries to build a stage.

title: QA_Platform_create_with_same_pr_line_twice_does_not_crash
preconditions: Caller is the QA buyer; {{productUuid}}/{{productQualityUuid}} are the client's catalog product. The request creates a NEW QA_Platform_ draft only; the PR reference is bogus so no real PR is touched.
steps: 1. POST /event_groups with two lines that both reference the same PR line (bogus id).
2. Read the status code.
expectedResult: No 5xx. CreateService does not de-duplicate PR references (create_service.rb:47-66), so today two lines point at one PR line; the duplicate is only caught when stages are built (one PRTM per EGLI) or when the line is pulled via pri_to_draft_project (existing_mapping, event_group_controller_helper.rb:84-87).
rationale: Same PR line twice in one event double-counts the requisition; records that the create path does not stop it.

title: QA_Platform_create_with_undecodable_pr_line_uuid_is_plain_draft
preconditions: Caller is the QA buyer; {{productUuid}}/{{productQualityUuid}} are the client's catalog product. The request creates a NEW QA_Platform_ draft only; the PR reference is bogus so no real PR is touched.
steps: 1. POST /event_groups with a line carrying pr_line_item_uuid = 'WrongUuid1=' (decodes to nothing).
2. Expect 200 and a draft with no PR link.
expectedResult: HTTP 200. ParamsAuth rewrites pr_line_item_uuid to pr_line_item_id = nil (params_auth.rb:74-75); the dormant gate compacts it away (create_service.rb:104-105) and set_pr_details finds nothing, so the result is an ordinary draft. The line's pr_line_item_id is null.
rationale: A garbled uuid from a stale cart must degrade to 'no PR link', not crash; the buyer then sees a non-PR draft.

title: QA_Platform_create_with_raw_numeric_pr_line_id_does_not_crash
preconditions: Caller is the QA buyer; {{productUuid}}/{{productQualityUuid}} are the client's catalog product. The request creates a NEW QA_Platform_ draft only; the PR reference is bogus so no real PR is touched.
steps: 1. POST /event_groups with a line carrying pr_line_item_id = 999999999 (raw integer, bypassing uuid decoding).
2. Read the status code.
expectedResult: No 5xx. Keys without 'uuid' are passed through untouched, so a raw id goes straight into the line's meta_data with no existence or company check (create_service.rb:47-66, trade_controller_helper.rb:6330). Only the dormant gate and set_pr_details are company-scoped, and both just skip it.
rationale: Raw-id references are how a client could point a draft at another tenant's PR line; records that create accepts them unchecked.

title: QA_Platform_create_with_text_pr_line_id_does_not_crash
preconditions: Caller is the QA buyer; {{productUuid}}/{{productQualityUuid}} are the client's catalog product. The request creates a NEW QA_Platform_ draft only; the PR reference is bogus so no real PR is touched.
steps: 1. POST /event_groups with a line carrying pr_line_item_id = 'QA_Platform_x_<stamp>' (not a number).
2. Read the status code.
expectedResult: No 5xx. The value reaches PurchaseRequestItem.where(id: [...]) in the dormant gate and set_pr_details (create_service.rb:79-81,111-113) - ActiveRecord casts a non-numeric string to NULL - and is then stored as-is in meta_data; the show serializer must not choke on it when it encodes the PR reference.
rationale: Unvalidated text in an id field; the risk is a 500 in the response serializer, not in the query.

title: QA_Platform_create_pr_line_with_zero_quantity_becomes_rate_only
preconditions: Caller is the QA buyer; {{productUuid}}/{{productQualityUuid}} are the client's catalog product. The request creates a NEW QA_Platform_ draft only; the PR reference is bogus so no real PR is touched.
steps: 1. POST /event_groups with a PR-referencing line whose quantity.value is 0.
2. Read the status code; if 200, the line is marked rate-only.
expectedResult: No 5xx. Zero (or null) quantity is not refused - get_details_for_event_group_line_items sets is_rate_only = true (trade_controller_helper.rb:6317-6320) - so a PR line becomes a rate-only line that reserves nothing on the PR.
rationale: Zero is the boundary between 'buy some' and 'ask for a rate'; a PR line silently turning rate-only means the PR stays fully open while an event exists for it.

title: QA_Platform_create_pr_line_with_negative_quantity_does_not_crash
preconditions: Caller is the QA buyer; {{productUuid}}/{{productQualityUuid}} are the client's catalog product. The request creates a NEW QA_Platform_ draft only; the PR reference is bogus so no real PR is touched.
steps: 1. POST /event_groups with a PR-referencing line whose quantity.value is -5.
2. Read the status code; a refusal is the desired answer.
expectedResult: No 5xx. There is no sign check anywhere on the create path (create_service.rb:47-66, trade_controller_helper.rb:6303-6320; EventGroupLineItem has no validations), so today -5 is stored. Desired: 422 refusal. If it is accepted, read the draft back and record the negative quantity as a defect.
rationale: A negative PR quantity, once published, is summed into the PR's in-progress quantity (purchase_request_item.rb:497-519) and would inflate the PR's open quantity.

title: QA_Platform_pr_list_with_open_and_in_progress_together_does_not_crash
preconditions: Caller is the QA buyer. Read only.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests?page=1 with filters {"status":["active","in_progress"]} (Open and In-progress at once).
2. Assert no 5xx.
expectedResult: Must not 5xx. SUSPECTED DEFECT: filter_by_status_and_get_quantities only assigns pr_items when status == ['active'] / ['approval_in_progress'] / ['in_progress'] exactly (app/services/purchase_requests/search_query.rb:402-413); any other mix that intersects that set returns nil, and the next line calls apply_scopes(nil, ...).distinct (app/services/purchase_requests/search_query.rb:112) - NoMethodError, untyped 500.
rationale: The PR list is the oracle for 'how much of this line is still open vs in an event'. A client (or report) asking for both buckets crashes the endpoint instead of getting the union.

title: QA_Platform_pr_list_with_unknown_status_does_not_crash
preconditions: Caller is the QA buyer. Read only.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests?page=1 with filters {"status":["QA_Platform_bogus"]}.
2. Assert no 5xx (an empty list or a 422 is fine).
expectedResult: Must not 5xx. SUSPECTED DEFECT: an unknown status matches none of the branches in filter_by_status_and_get_quantities (app/services/purchase_requests/search_query.rb:400-421), which then returns nil as the relation; the following apply_scopes(...).distinct (app/services/purchase_requests/search_query.rb:112) raises NoMethodError.
rationale: Unknown enum values in filters should narrow to nothing, not crash; a renamed tab key on the client would take the PR page down.

title: QA_Platform_pr_list_with_status_as_text_does_not_crash
preconditions: Caller is the QA buyer. Read only.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests?page=1 with filters {"status":"active"} (a string, not an array).
2. Assert no 5xx.
expectedResult: Must not 5xx. SUSPECTED DEFECT: ["active","in_progress","approval_in_progress"] & "active" raises TypeError (no implicit conversion of String into Array) at app/services/purchase_requests/search_query.rb:402; nothing rescues it. ViewService already tolerates a string status (view_service.rb:100-102) but SearchQuery runs first.
rationale: Every other PR filter is shape-tolerant; this one is not, and the dashboard's own view-service code shows a string status is expected input.

title: QA_Platform_pr_list_with_unknown_closure_type_does_not_crash
preconditions: Caller is the QA buyer. Read only.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests?page=1 with filters {"status":["completed"],"closure_type":["QA_Platform_bogus"]}.
2. Assert no 5xx.
expectedResult: Must not 5xx. SUSPECTED DEFECT: an unknown closure type falls to the else-branch of filter_by_closure_type, collects no ids, and returns `... if combined_ids.any?` = nil (app/services/purchase_requests/search_query.rb:530-537); the chain then reaches nil.order(...) (app/services/purchase_requests/search_query.rb:143) - NoMethodError.
rationale: Closure type is how a buyer finds partially-closed vs PO-closed lines in the Completed tab; a typo must give an empty page, not an error page.

title: QA_Platform_pr_list_partial_closure_filter_reads_cleanly
preconditions: Caller is the QA buyer. Read only. Behaviour differs with is_pr_partial_closure_enabled; both answers are 200.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests?page=1 with filters {"status":["completed"],"closure_type":["partial_closure"]}.
2. Assert no 5xx; note whether the list is narrowed.
expectedResult: HTTP 200. With the partial-closure feature off, 'partial_closure' is stripped from the filter and the Completed list comes back UNFILTERED (app/services/purchase_requests/search_query.rb:512-515) - a silent widening rather than an empty result. With it on, only lines carrying partial_closure_metadata are returned.
rationale: Records the silent-widening behaviour: a report built on this filter would count every completed line when the feature is off.

title: QA_Platform_pr_list_filtered_by_a_non_pr_event_is_empty
preconditions: Caller is the QA buyer. Read only. The sandbox {{eventGroupUuid}} was built from the catalog, not from a PR.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests?page=1 with filters {"status":["in_progress"],"rfx_uuids":["{{eventGroupUuid}}"]}.
2. Assert no 5xx and an empty purchase_requests list.
expectedResult: HTTP 200 with no rows: parse_filters turns rfx_uuids into rfx_ids (common_functions.rb:93) and the rfx_ids scope joins PR lines to that event group (purchase_request_item.rb:282); the sandbox has no PR mapping. (If the uuid contains '+', the query string turns it into a space and the decode yields nil - still an empty 200.)
rationale: Read-back oracle for 'which PR lines does this event consume' - the call a test uses after pulling lines in; it must be exact and must not crash on a non-PR event.

title: QA_Platform_pr_list_rfx_id_wildcard_does_not_crash
preconditions: Caller is the QA buyer. Read only.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests?page=1 with filters {"status":["in_progress"],"rfx_id_ilike":"%"}.
2. Assert no 5xx.
expectedResult: HTTP 200. The value is bound (no injection) but '%'/'_' are not escaped in the rfx_id_ilike scope (purchase_request_item.rb:283-286), so '%' matches every PR line linked to any event - a wildcard, not a literal search.
rationale: Records that event-reference search treats % and _ as wildcards (unlike rfq_no, which goes through sql_like).

title: QA_Platform_pr_list_unknown_event_status_does_not_crash
preconditions: Caller is the QA buyer. Read only.
steps: 1. GET /purchase_requests?page=1 with filters {"status":["in_progress"],"event_statuses":["QA_Platform_bogus"]}.
2. Assert no 5xx and an empty list.
expectedResult: HTTP 200, empty. event_statuses is a jsonb ?| ARRAY[...] bind (purchase_request_item.rb:256-268); an unknown value simply matches nothing.
rationale: The 'event status' column filter on In-progress is how a buyer finds PR lines whose event was awarded; unknown values must be harmless.

title: QA_Platform_pr_number_options_wildcard_search_does_not_crash
preconditions: Caller is the QA buyer. Read only.
steps: 1. GET /event_groups/pr_number_options?page=1&search_query=% .
2. Assert no 5xx.
expectedResult: HTTP 200 with PR numbers linked to ACTIVE events only (filter_options_helper.rb:38-53). The search is a bound ILIKE but '%' is not escaped, so it returns everything.
rationale: This options list feeds the event list's 'PR number' filter; it must stay read-only and crash-free on wildcard input.

title: QA_Platform_pr_number_options_negative_page_is_clamped
preconditions: Caller is the QA buyer. Read only.
steps: 1. GET /event_groups/pr_number_options?page=-5.
2. Assert no 5xx and the first page returned.
expectedResult: HTTP 200, first page: EventGroupsController#paginate clamps with [1, page.to_i].max (app/controllers/api/event_groups_controller.rb:1703-1705).
rationale: Negative paging must clamp, not raise in Kaminari.

title: QA_Platform_partial_close_without_reason_is_refused_for_a_real_line
preconditions: is_pr_partial_closure_enabled is ON (enabled: true). {{prItemId}} is a REAL PR line; the body has no closure_reason, which no configured reason key can match, so the request is refused before any write.
steps: 1. PATCH /purchase_requests/partial_close with pr_item_uuids = [a real PR line] (the key the dashboard sends), remarks set, and NO closure_reason.
2. Read the status code and error.
3. GET /purchase_requests/{{prId}} - the line has no partial_closure_metadata.
expectedResult: HTTP 422, error.code 2 with message 'Invalid closure reason'. The controller coerces params[:closure_reason].to_s to '' (purchase_requests_controller.rb:1006) and validate checks allowed_closure_reason_keys.include?('') (app/services/purchase_requests/partial_closure_service.rb:154) before the item lookup. With the feature off the answer is 861 instead.
rationale: Uses the dashboard's real key (pr_item_uuids, decoded by ParamsAuth) - unlike the older PR-PCL cases that send uuids under pr_item_ids, which never decode and can only ever reach 528. Proves a closure without a reason is impossible on a real line.

title: QA_Platform_partial_close_with_markup_only_remarks_is_refused
preconditions: Caller is the QA buyer; the line id is bogus (Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==), so even a regressed validator cannot close anything (528 at worst).
steps:
1. PATCH /purchase_requests/partial_close with remarks = '

' (markup only), a plausible reason key and a bogus line.
2. Read the status code.
expectedResult: Non-2xx, never 5xx: 861 (feature off), 2 'Invalid closure reason' (reason not configured), 2 'Remarks are required' (sanitize_input_params strips the tags, params_auth.rb:18-30, leaving a blank string caught at app/services/purchase_requests/partial_closure_service.rb:155) or 528 (line not found). Which one depends on the company's closure_reasons list.
rationale: The UI trims remarks before sending (partiallyClosedDrawer.jsx:51-52); the API must reach the same verdict when the only content is markup.

title: QA_Platform_partial_close_with_reason_as_object_is_refused
preconditions: is_pr_partial_closure_enabled is ON (enabled: true). {{prItemId}} is a REAL PR line; the reason is an object, so no configured key can match.
steps: 1. PATCH /purchase_requests/partial_close with closure_reason = {"key":"budget_cut"} (object instead of the key string).
2. Read the status code and error.
expectedResult: HTTP 422, error.code 2 with message 'Invalid closure reason' - .to_s turns the Parameters object into its inspect string (purchase_requests_controller.rb:1006), which is not a configured key (app/services/purchase_requests/partial_closure_service.rb:154). Not a 500 from the Sorbet String sig.
rationale: A client posting the whole reason option (key + label) instead of the key is a realistic bug; it must get a readable refusal.

title: QA_Platform_partial_close_with_comma_separated_uuid_string_is_refused
preconditions: is_pr_partial_closure_enabled is ON (enabled: true). Bogus line ids only.
steps: 1. PATCH /purchase_requests/partial_close with pr_item_uuids = 'Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==,Z2dnWmdaUWtnZw==' (one string) and an unconfigurable reason.
2. Read the status code and error.
expectedResult: HTTP 422, error.code 2 with message 'Invalid closure reason'. ParamsAuth splits a *_uuids STRING on commas and decodes each (params_auth.rb:72-73), so this is accepted as two ids, de-duplicated to one (app/services/purchase_requests/partial_closure_service.rb:36), and stopped at the reason rung (app/services/purchase_requests/partial_closure_service.rb:154).
rationale: Documents the undocumented comma-string form of every *_uuids parameter and that it does not crash the closure service.

title: QA_Platform_partial_close_with_ids_as_object_is_refused
preconditions: is_pr_partial_closure_enabled is ON (enabled: true). Bogus ids only.
steps: 1. PATCH /purchase_requests/partial_close with pr_item_ids = {"a": 999999999} (an object) and an unconfigurable reason.
2. Read the status code and error.
expectedResult: HTTP 422, error.code 2 with message 'Invalid closure reason'. Array(params[:pr_item_ids]) wraps the object as a one-element array (purchase_requests_controller.rb:1005); it is not blank and not over 20, so the reason rung answers (app/services/purchase_requests/partial_closure_service.rb:152-154). Not a 500.
rationale: Type confusion on the id list must not escape as a 500 from Array()/uniq or the Sorbet sig.

title: QA_Platform_partial_close_without_any_line_ids_is_refused
preconditions: is_pr_partial_closure_enabled is ON (enabled: true). No line ids at all.
steps: 1. PATCH /purchase_requests/partial_close with only closure_reason and remarks (no pr_item_ids / pr_item_uuids key).
2. Read the status code and error.
expectedResult: HTTP 422, error.code 2 'Insufficient parameters' - Array(nil) is [] and validate's first rung is @pr_item_ids.blank? (app/services/purchase_requests/partial_closure_service.rb:152), which runs before the reason check.
rationale: Missing (not empty) id list; confirms the 2 comes from the first rung so the reason/remarks rungs are never reached.
